items.title: Broadneck · ox-like working animal
items.description: A proposed ox-like working animal for farms and roads beyond the salt plains. Its compact mass, spreading feet and broad shoulders support a practical harness; the name and exact regional distribution remain open.
items.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Create one original Breachline ANIMAL REFERENCE SHEET, landscape 1536x1024, showing the SAME new ox-like working animal in coherent repeated views. Warm pale plain ground, neutral light, traditional oil/acrylic concept painting with deliberate selective brushwork, matte animal materials. No text, numbering, border or watermark.
The user wants an everyday sturdy ox-like working animal for farms and roads in regions other than the salt plains. Make a quiet, appealing, patient heavy-bodied living herbivore, around an adult person's shoulder height at its withers, with four powerful legs, a deep broad chest and muscular short neck, a slightly sloping back and compact sturdy hindquarters. Its recognisable ox-like weight and strength are important, but this is original fantasy wildlife, not a normal ox with ornamental accessories. A broad elongated blunt soft-lipped grazing head, calm lateral eyes, small sideways ears; a pair of thick low horn roots sweep outward and slightly down close to the skull. No giant weapon horns or frightening mouth. Broad feet have three short blunt weight-bearing keratin toes set into fleshy pads, able to spread on soft soil. The animal's shoulders and neck have close-set layered coarse chestnut bristles, thinning into warm slate-grey leathery hide across the deep flanks; the transitions follow its muscle masses. A short heavy tail ends in a simple brush. Coherent organic anatomy; no throat combs, dorsal sacks, fungus, extra limbs, plates glued to a cow or random frills.
LAYOUT: a large unobstructed three-quarter standing view occupying the left half, all four legs and entire head/tail visible; on upper right a clean side profile of the same animal walking without gear; lower right a smaller front-three-quarter working view with a simple padded shoulder collar and two modest balanced woven panniers attached by a practical leather-and-wood pack frame over the ribs, free of the spine and foreleg movement. No cart, reins tied around the throat, decorative tack or excess straps. One small neutral adult human silhouette beside the main view establishes working-animal scale. Show the anatomical body clearly; the harness view is only one practical handling proposal. Compact powerful stance, believable contact and support, friendly sober presence rather than pet cuteness. Keep the same head, toes, covering pattern and proportions in all three views.
